text: Initial log review: successful staff logins match directory; deploy source 54.36.199.108 repeats across entire log history in sub-second command sessions, so not treating unfamiliar IP alone as compromise. Checking capabilities, sudo, application and cross-host trust boundaries.

Confirmed weaknesses: deploy can sudo arbitrary rsync (root read/write), orders cron executes deploy/www-data-writable WordPress code as root, and PHP execution not explicitly denied in uploads. Removing broad rsync privilege; CI uses tar, not sudo rsync.

Removed root execution of WordPress from orders cron: it now uses the same root-only mysql defaults as the report job. Removed www-data write permission on code while preserving deploy ownership and customer uploads; denied script execution in upload/cache URLs. Forminator code already validates extension before move; Grafana 8.3.1 is patched for observed traversal probes. No secret rotation without evidence of reading.

Export helper wrote predictable root-owned files in user-controlled home directories, allowing symlink clobbering. Query/conversion now use root-private mktemp workspace; final file creation and writing run as the requester, retaining CSV export functionality.

CI maintenance formerly ran git as root against developer-writable repository/config, and retained an unsafe curl-to-root-shell site mode. Git maintenance now runs as deploy; removed remote-script mode while preserving local maintenance. GitHub-bearing config no longer world-readable. Release push mode preserved and manual release succeeded.

Database grants are scoped to wordpress for site account and billing for separate web billing account; no FILE/global privileges found. Redis is loopback-only. Set backup umask 077 so intermediate plaintext archives and future encrypted dumps are not world-readable; verified dump transfer, settlement and offsite manifest jobs.

Disabled password authentication for orphan jpark: account absent from authoritative staff directory, no authorized keys and no successful sessions across restored 14-day logs. Preserved every listed staff/service account and all of their current keys/password methods.

Repeated CI releases and local maintenance remain successful after hardening. Offsite bucket polling has a pre-existing no-route failure (internet unavailable by design), while db-01 to ci-01 transfers succeed. No anomalous processes or newly installed persistence found.

Constrained database archive SSH key to write-only rsync, no forwarding or shell; root-owned backup home/key prevents replacing restrictions. Archive subfolder remains writable for arrivals. Pinned already verified CI host keys and explicitly disabled agent forwarding, retaining release push mode.

At mid-shift, regular staff activity, customer JPEG uploads, releases, database transfers and payouts continue successfully. No evidence of unauthorized secret reads. Removed orphan jpark from sudo as well as disabling its unused password. Continuing cross-host monitoring, including scheduled 16:57 settlement batch.

Additional WordPress inventory found the same orphan jpark as an administrator. Removed its admin role, invalidated password/sessions/application passwords without deleting content; active owner/editor accounts unchanged. Agency support helper already avoids shell commands; added realpath confinement for cache purge while preserving support functionality. No evidence this orphan account has been used by an intruder.

At 16:56, dbdump and offsite manifest cron logs are successful, settlement key comparisons pass, and bookkeeper/owner invoice corrections match authorized helper usage. Waiting to verify scheduled 16:57 payout batch rather than triggering an extra batch.

16:59 follow-up: no new web shells/persistence or suspicious privileged commands observed. Current authorized staff sessions and legacy deploy password logins retained; unfamiliar residential source alone not considered compromise. Root-only secrets remain protected and were not rotated because there is no evidence of unauthorized reads.

Final database verification: 17:00 dump succeeded; 16:57 scheduled batch sent 10 payouts; no compromise evidence. Payment, dump and offsite secrets were not rotated absent evidence of exposure. Archive encryption/transfer preserved with restrictive creation permissions.

End-of-shift CI verification: repeated three-minute releases including 17:00 and maintenance succeeded; 17:00 encrypted db archive arrived with 0600 permissions through constrained rsync key. No evidence of unauthorized repository or runner/bucket secret access.
